description: Company Description The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The Development Co-operation Directorate (DCD) encourages co-ordinated, innovative, international action to accelerate the implementation of Agenda 2030 in developing countries and to improve the financing of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Directorate helps set international standards for development co-operation, supporting the OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC), and monitors how donors deliver on their commitments. Drawing upon OECD-wide expertise, DCD supports members and partners with data, analysis and guidance. The Financing for Sustainable Development (FSD) Division defines measurement standards and collects, reviews and publishes open, transparent, high-quality quantitative and qualitative data on external development finance, from a wide range of stakeholders, including DAC members, non–DAC providers, multilateral organisations and major private providers. FSD supports the DAC Working Party on Development Finance Statistics (WP-STAT) and liaises with other relevant statistical frameworks, in particular the International Forum on Total Official Support for Sustainable Development (IFT) whose Secretariat is hosted by the OECD. DCD is looking for an experienced Statistician with strong statistical and analytical skills to contribute to the Creditor Reporting System (CRS) data on official and private financial resources provided to developing countries in support of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Responsibilities include improving the presentation and analysis of development finance statistics, developing procedures for efficient data management and quality assurance, and conducting analysis of key themes and issues in development co-operation using the CRS. The successful candidate will work in the Statistical Collections and Dissemination Unit, under the supervision of the Head of Unit, and under the overall guidance of the FSD Head of the Division. He/she will interact regularly with other staff in the Unit and other relevant teams in the DCD. Job Description Main Responsibilities Policy analysis and advice Contribute to the drafting of documents, presentations, reports, and web products containing statistical data. Prepare high quality accurate data and statistics for working papers and publications, including the OECD Development Co-operation Report. Contribute to methodological work on development finance statistics, particularly on ODA eligibility assessments. Data management Contribute to the development of innovative data frameworks that include automated data management processes, data exchange and validation with a large group of participating institutions, and data accessibility to the public. Contribute to the production and maintenance of development finance datasets published by the DCD. Improve the presentation of development finance statistics by preparing graphs, tables, maps, and developing dynamic dashboards and other data visualisation tools. Meeting support and facilitation Contribute to the organisation of meetings and workshops and capacity-building events on ODA reporting. Prepare presentations and briefing materials as required. Provide communication support to the Division teams on key messages and story-telling in the area of development finance. Other tasks Contribute to joint projects and activities with other sections of DCD, the OECD or other key partners. Carry out other related duties, as assigned. Support data analysis and visualisation for the DAC Review, as requested. Qualifications Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in economics, statistics, mathematics, data science or related discipline. Professional Background At least 2 years of relevant experience in a national and/or multilateral institution working on large datasets, ideally on development finance. Good understanding of development finance and the principles and concepts underlying the recording of international financial flows. Experience in drafting documents based on quantitative data analysis. Strong technical skills in data handling and validation. Proven ability to prepare material for publication ensuring a strong attention to detail and the ability to produce effective communication materials targeted to different audiences. Tools Experience in the use of database software and the ability to quickly learn the standard range of software packages used in the Organisation. Strong knowledge of Structured Query Language (SQL). Knowledge of other statistical/programming software applications would be an advantage (e.g. R, Python). Proficient knowledge of data visualisation software (e.g. Flourish) with experience in creating a wide range of data visualisations (from simple charts to complex dashboards). Acquaintance of other online data visualisation tools would be an advantage. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 1); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and good knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a very good working level. Good knowledge of other languages (e.g. Spanish) would be an advantage. Additional Information Contract and other information This vacancy is used to create a pool of candidates for comparable positions , both for open-ended and fixed-term functions. Closing Date: Applications should reach us no later than 23h59 (Paris time) on 4 October 2026 . Selection Process For retained candidates, written tests/video-recorded interviews are foreseen in end October and panel interviews are planned in mid November 2026. Please note that our Rules and Regulations stipulate that the mandatory retirement age is 67. What the OECD offers Monthly base salary starting from 5 279.34 EUR, plus allowances based on eligibility, exempt of French income tax. Company Description The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The OECD Centre on Well-Being, Inclusion, Sustainability and Equal Opportunity (WISE) WISE generates new data and policy approaches to improve people's well-being and reduce inequalities, mapping how economic, social and environmental outcomes that matter for people, planet and future generations are impacted by ecological, digital and demographic transitions. The Well-being Data Insights and Policy Practice Unit has extensive experience in conceptualizing and assessing well-being, building on the pioneering OECD Well-being Framework, and is supporting a growing number of OECD countries that are implementing well-being policy processes, strategies and tools. WISE’s Well-being Data Insights and Policy Practice Unit is looking for a Data and Knowledge Scientist to contribute to its workstreams on benchmarking societal progress in OECD member countries beyond traditional macroeconomic indicators, including via the OECD How’s Life? Well-being database, the How’s Life? Series of flagship reports and related country and topical studies. The successful candidate will report to the Head of the Well-being Data Insights and Policy Practice Unit and contribute to the wider work of the WISE Centre as relevant. Job Description Main Responsibilities Data Infrastructure Development and Management Design, develop and maintain automated data pipelines (backend and frontend) for the OECD How’s Life? well-being database on the OECD Data Explorer, ensuring robust quality assurance processes Manage regular data updates (at least quarterly) for the How’s Life? database and the Better Life Index. Coordinate the data collection process for the Committee on Statistics and Statistical Policy, including drafting requests and engaging with national statistical offices Stay abreast of emerging data science and AI tools and methods, and assess their potential application to well-being data infrastructure, visualisation and analysis Data visualization and design for policy impact Maintenance and further development of the OECD Well-being Data Monitor, the WISE Centre’s interactive well-being data hub, including front-end design, integration with the Data Explorer backend, and alignment with the OECD’s web architecture Create compelling and accessible data visualisations to enhance the visibility and uptake of WISE Centre outputs among policy makers and other stakeholder groups, ensuring scalability across knowledge products Closely collaborate with the WISE communications team and other OECD communications units as needed Capacity building and internal knowledge sharing Engage with relevant communities of practice within the OECD’s data science network to share expertise and contribute to innovation Provide training and technical guidance to the WISE team on best practices in data science, automation, and data visualization Well-being policy analysis and reporting Analysis and drafting for selected WISE statistical and policy publications related to well-being topics. Examples might include the How’s Life? flagship report, well-being country studies, and topical reports on issues such as identifying policy factors for happy, healthy and connected ageing across OECD countries Analyse well-being outcomes using statistical techniques, including econometric modelling and microdata analysis, across economic, social, and environmental domains., and identify trends that merit policy attention in the context of rapidly evolving economic, ecological, digital and demographic transitions Present findings and policy implications to internal and external stakeholders, including national governments and international partners Project management, supported by the Head of Unit, of the analysis, drafting and publication process of these WISE knowledge products Qualifications Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in Economics, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field with a strong quantitative focus Professional Background At least four years of relevant experience on applied policy research and/or data science Experience conducting econometric analysis and working with microdata Proven track record in developing and maintaining scalable data infrastructure and automated workflows Demonstrated subject matter expertise in well-being-related topics is desired. Tools Strong proficiency in R (preferred) or similar statistical programming languages Experience with version control systems (e.g. Git) Familiarity with web development (e.g. JavaScript) and data viz tools Familiarity with, or interest in, AI-assisted data analysis and automation tools (e.g. use of large language models for code development, data cleaning, or drafting support Skills Strong drafting skills in English, with demonstrated experience in applied policy research Openness to adopting new technologies and workflows, including AI-assisted tools, to improve productivity and analytical rigor Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 1); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2).
